Imported hosts are stored un-normalized because the raw SQL INSERT bypasses the model's before_validation that strips http(s):// prefixes and paths, so previously-working hosts with scheme prefixes silently stop matching after upgrade

Unescaped interpolation of host strings from the site setting into SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) aborts the migration on values containing single quotes and creates a SQL-injection surface fed from admin-editable data

Validation regex allows hosts with ports (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) but record_for_host compares the port-less uri.host of the referer, so saved port-bearing hosts pass validation yet can never allow embedding

Validation regex requires domain.tld format, rejecting single-label hosts (localhost), IP addresses, and TLDs longer than 5 chars (.travel, .online) that the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? previously accepted — a regression for valid configurations
before_validation calls self.host.sub! unguarded, so a nil host (e.g. missing param via direct API call) raises NoMethodError producing a 500 instead of a clean validation error

Client/server category divergence: for new hosts categoryId starts null and the success handler sets host.category = Discourse.Category.findById(null) (falsy), making the badge disappear and the next edit() read host.category.id as undefined, so UI state diverges from what was persisted

Hot-path host check regressed from in-memory lookup to a per-request DB query: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? (record_for_host) issues a Postgres query on every call instead of the previous in-memory SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? check, adding DB load and latency to every /embed/comments and /embed/count request and each imported post, with no memoization or cache invalidated on host create/update/destroy

Lookup query is non-sargable and the embeddable_hosts table has no index: where("lower(host) = ?", host) cannot use a plain btree index and the migration creates no index on host, forcing a sequential scan on every lookup; normalizing hosts to lowercase in before_validation with where(host: host) or adding an expression index on lower(host) would fix it

Migration interpolates unescaped setting values into SQL: the INSERT for embeddable_hosts uses string interpolation of h from the old free-form embeddable_hosts setting, so any value containing a single quote or backslash breaks the statement and crashes the migration

For PostgreSQL `PG::Result`, `cmd_tuples` reflects rows affected by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (SELECT typically yields 0), so this guard can prevent the import block from ever running even when the SELECT returns a row. The migration then unconditionally executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, which would drop the existing configuration without having inserted it into `embeddable_hosts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation regex allows hosts with ports (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) but record_for_host compares the port-less uri.host of the referer, so saved port-bearing hosts pass validation yet can never allow embedding

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`). The `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not remove a port, so a record like `example.com:3000` can be saved. However, `record_for_host` parses the referer with `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (which omits the port) and compares it to the stored `host` via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means a stored host containing a port will never match a referer for the same hostname, making embedding effectively impossible for such saved entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation regex requires domain.tld format, rejecting single-label hosts (localhost), IP addresses, and TLDs longer than 5 chars (.travel, .online) that the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? previously accepted — a regression for valid configurations

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model enforces `validates_format_of :host` with a regex that requires a dotted domain and restricts the TLD to 2–5 chars (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), which will reject single-label hosts like `localhost`, IP addresses, and modern longer TLDs like `.online`/`.travel` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` logic did not enforce such a regex and would accept arbitrary host strings via string/URI parsing (app/models/site_setting.rb removed block), so this is a behavior regression introduced by the diff.

destroyRecord().then(...) in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch (unlike save which uses popupAjaxError), so a failed DELETE leaves the row in place with no user feedback and an unhandled rejection

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but provides no `.catch(...)` handler. Unlike `save()`, which does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, a failed DELETE would produce an unhandled rejection and no user-visible error. The row also won’t be removed because `sendAction('deleteHost', ...)` only runs in the success `then` callback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client/server category divergence: for new hosts categoryId starts null and the success handler sets host.category = Discourse.Category.findById(null) (falsy), making the badge disappear and the next edit() read host.category.id as undefined, so UI state diverges from what was persisted

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `categoryId` is initialized to `null` and for a new host there is no `edit()` call to populate it. On `save()`, it sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` (so `null`), while the server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) replaces blank `category_id` with `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` and persists that. However, the client success handler then does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));` which becomes `findById(null)` and will set `host.category` to a falsy/undefined value, diverging from the persisted category. The template (`{{category-badge host.category}}`) would then lose the badge, and later `edit()` does `this.get('host.category.id')` which can be `undefined` if `host.category` was cleared.

EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? calls record_for_host, which runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`—a DB query on each invocation. The diff shows no caching/memoization and no invalidation hooks beyond normal CRUD, so the performance/latency concern is real, but it’s not a correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lookup query is non-sargable and the embeddable_hosts table has no index: where("lower(host) = ?", host) cannot use a plain btree index and the migration creates no index on host, forcing a sequential scan on every lookup; normalizing hosts to lowercase in before_validation with where(host: host) or adding an expression index on lower(host) would fix it

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` using `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), and the migration creating `embeddable_hosts` does not add any index on `host` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). Without an index, lookups like `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (used in EmbedController and TopicRetriever) will require scanning the table; and even if a plain btree index were added on `host`, the `lower(host)` expression would not use it unless you normalize stored values or add an expression index. This is a concrete performance/maintainability issue introduced by the change, but not a correctness/security defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes when embed_category was never saved: the site_settings query returns zero rows on most sites and fresh DBs, causing NoMethodError on [0]['id'] and blocking the upgrade entirely; the fallback query for uncategorized_category_id has the same unguarded pattern, and the query also fails if the saved value no longer exactly matches a category name

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` unconditionally does `execute(...)[0]['id']` when looking up the old `embed_category` (and similarly `execute(...)[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id`). If those queries return 0 rows (e.g., `embed_category` was never set, or the join `s.value = c.name` finds no match), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']`/`nil['value']` will raise `NoMethodError`, blocking upgrades. The join also depends on the stored value exactly matching a category name, which can fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates unescaped setting values into SQL: the INSERT for embeddable_hosts uses string interpolation of h from the old free-form embeddable_hosts setting, so any value containing a single quote or backslash breaks the statement and crashes the migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes directly from the old `site_settings` value (`val.split("\n")`). There is no quoting/escaping (e.g., `quote(h)`), so a host containing a single quote/backslash will produce invalid SQL and can crash the migration (and is also SQL-injection-prone in principle, even if settings are admin-controlled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrated hosts are not normalized: the migration copies raw values (e.g. http://example.com) into the table bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison never matches and embedding silently breaks for previously-working sites after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` copies each line from the old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` directly into the `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`). This bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If migrated rows contain values like `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, they will not equal `uri.host` (e.g. `example.com`), causing `host_allowed?` to return false and breaking embedding for previously-allowed hosts after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`), which will raise `NoMethodError` if the `:embeddable_host` wrapper is missing. Separately, `EmbeddableHost` has a `before_validation` block that unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`), which will raise if `host` is nil. Both cases would yield a 500 rather than a normal validation/error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hosts saved with a port can never match: the validation regex allows example.com:8080 but record_for_host compares against URI(...).host which never includes a port, so embedding from that host is silently denied and TopicEmbed.import gets no category

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows storing a host with an optional port (e.g. `example.com:8080`). The `before_validation` hook strips scheme and path but does not remove the port, so the DB can contain `host = "example.com:8080"`. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and compares using `uri.host` (hostname only, no port) in `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so `example.com` will never match a stored `example.com:8080`. This would cause `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to deny such referers and `TopicEmbed.import` to fail to find the embeddable host/category when URLs include a port.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host validation regex rejects legitimate hosts: \.[a-z]{2,5} rejects TLDs longer than 5 chars (.online, .technology), single-label hosts like localhost, and IP addresses — a functional regression since the old site setting accepted free-form values

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `EmbeddableHost` model with `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). This validation will reject hosts with TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. `.technology`, `.online`), single-label hosts like `localhost` (no dot), and IP addresses. Previously, embeddable hosts were stored as free-form site setting lines and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` compared parsed hosts without such TLD-length/single-label constraints (app/models/site_setting.rb removed). Since admin create/update now uses `host.save` (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb), these legitimate values can no longer be added/edited, making this a behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client delete() in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no error handling: destroyRecord().then(...) lacks a .catch (unlike save() which uses popupAjaxError), so on failure the user gets no feedback and the row silently remains

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which ends with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the delete request fails, no error is surfaced to the user and no recovery/rollback path is triggered, resulting in a silent failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store plural-id hydration destroys unmatched _ids keys: the plural branch unconditionally deletes obj[k] and sets obj[pluralize(subType)] to the mapped array, so any payload with a xxx_ids attribute not accompanied by a sideloaded xxxs collection loses the ids and gets an array of undefined — a latent hazard for all store consumers

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` when `m[2]` is truthy) always does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and then unconditionally `delete obj[k]`. If the payload contains e.g. `color_ids: [1,2]` but the sideloaded `colors` collection is missing or incomplete, `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined`, producing `[undefined, ...]` while also deleting the original `*_ids` list. This is a real behavior change vs the singular branch (which only deletes the key when hydration succeeds) and can cause loss of information / broken relationships for store consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? guard removed and its test is now vacuous: the host-existence condition in topic.rb was dropped so first-post expansion is no longer gated on any embeddable host being configured, and the rewritten test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes for the wrong reason, leaving the removed condition untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the embeddable-hosts presence guard in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (topic.rb changes from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && ...` to just `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). The rewritten spec case `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer stubs `has_topic_embed?` or sets `SiteSetting.embed_truncate`, so it will pass simply because defaults make the method return false, not because any “no host configured” condition is enforced. Whether the guard removal is a product bug is not verifiable from the diff, but the test becoming vacuous is directly supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup for embeddable_hosts.category_id when a category is deleted: belongs_to :category has no dependent handling and no FK, leaving dangling category_id values that flow into TopicEmbed.import and the serializer/admin UI, potentially causing wrong/uncategorized categorization or failed imports

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces EmbeddableHost with a non-null `category_id` column (migration `create_table :embeddable_hosts ... t.integer :category_id, null: false`) and a plain `belongs_to :category` with no DB FK and no on-delete handling. However, the diff does not show how category deletion is handled elsewhere (it may be prevented or cleaned up globally), so the failure mode is not strictly verifiable from this diff alone.

If the SELECT returns no rows (e.g., setting unset, deleted, or value doesn’t match any `categories.name`), `[0]` is `nil` and `['id']` will raise NoMethodError/IndexError before the `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. If any host line contains a single quote (or other SQL-special characters), the SQL becomes invalid and the migration can fail; it also creates SQL-injection risk from unescaped setting content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration join assumes embed_category stored a category name; if it stored a category id, every migrated host silently falls back to uncategorized

If an existing install stored something else (e.g., an id, slug, etc.), the query yields no rows and `category_id` becomes 0, triggering the fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, potentially mis-migrating host-category mappings. adjudication_records.issue_text: Hosts with a port pass validation and are saved, but record_for_host compares against URI(url).host which never includes a port, so port-qualified hosts can never allow embedding and no test covers ports

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex permits an optional port (`...(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` callback strips protocol and path but does not remove the port (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Store plural hydration: 'hydrated || []' is dead code because map() always returns an array

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural hydration branch in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always produce an Array (and `[]` is truthy), so `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];` will always take `hydrated` and the `|| []` fallback is effectively unnecessary. adjudication_records.issue_text: Store plural hydration throws on a null obj[k] (obj[k].map), whereas the singular path tolerates falsy values via if (hydrated)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded` now matches plural keys via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and, when plural (`m[2]` truthy), unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If the server returns a null/undefined value for a `*_ids` field, this will throw (`Cannot read property 'map' of null/undefined`). The singular branch guards via `if (hydrated)` before assignment/deletion, so it tolerates falsy values better. This is a real, diff-introduced runtime defect risk in the new plural hydration path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store plural hydration with an unknown/unresolvable subtype stores [undefined] and deletes the raw *_ids key, unlike the singular path which preserves the raw key on failed hydration — a behavioral asymmetry that discards data

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`) always does `delete obj[k]` after setting `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `hydrated` is an array returned from `obj[k].map(...)`, it will include `undefined` entries when `_lookupSubType(...)` can’t resolve an id (no filtering), and the original raw `*_ids` array is discarded regardless. By contrast, the singular path only deletes the raw `*_id` key when hydration succeeds (`if (hydrated) { ... delete obj[k]; }`). This is a verifiable asymmetry introduced by the diff and can lose the original ids.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import with no matching host record now creates the topic with no category since the global embed_category setting was removed; callers like feed-polling imports previously landed in the configured embed category — behavior change with no test pinning the no-match path

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: `_hydrateEmbedded` plural branch is unguarded, changing global behavior — the `_ids` branch calls `obj[k].map(...)` without verifying the value is an array (a `foo_ids: null` payload throws) and always assigns the mapped array and deletes the original key, so when the sideloaded collection isn't in the root consumers get `[undefined, …]` and raw ids are gone; applies to every REST payload, not just embedding (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` was changed to also match `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and the plural branch (`if (m[2])`) now unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)` and then `delete obj[k]`. There is no check that `obj[k]` is an array, so a payload like `foo_ids: null` / missing key will throw at `.map`. Also, it always replaces the raw `*_ids` with `pluralize(subType)` even if `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for some/all ids (e.g., sideloaded collection not present in `root`), producing `[undefined, ...]` and removing the original ids. Since `_hydrateEmbedded` runs for all REST payloads, this is a global behavior change, not limited to embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore — works for `embeddable_host` but any future admin model with two or more underscores won't match ADMIN_MODELS and will silently get non-admin base paths; should be `.replace(/_/g, '-')` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `basePath` to normalize `type` via `type.replace('_', '-')` before checking membership in `ADMIN_MODELS` (rest.js.es6). In JavaScript, `String#replace` with a string pattern only replaces the first occurrence, so a type like `foo_bar_baz` would become `foo-bar_baz` and fail to match an `ADMIN_MODELS` entry like `foo-bar-baz`, resulting in a non-admin base path. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness issue, but the diff only introduces/uses `embeddable-host` (single underscore case), so no currently-shown behavior is broken.
